name: Pingcore
description:
Connect Claude to PingCore to build, deploy, scale, monitor, and manage multiplayer game server infrastructure through natural language.

The PingCore MCP server gives Claude access to PingCore’s API documentation, OpenAPI schemas, workflow guides, and infrastructure management tools. Use it to generate integration code, deploy game servers across global locations, scale deployments, restart or reconfigure servers, inspect player counts, monitor memory usage, troubleshoot issues, and automate common operational workflows.

PingCore is built for game studios, hosting providers, and developers running multiplayer servers at scale, with support for pre-configured games, container-based deployments, global infrastructure, real-time monitoring, and gaming-focused DDoS protection.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Pingcore to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Pingcore to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://pingcore.io/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Pingcore MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pingcore lists 49 MCP tools, including acknowledge_manual_mod, check_mod_updates, create_server, create_server_config, create_server_task, delete_server, delete_server_config, delete_server_task, get_guide, get_mod_details, get_mod_download_url, and get_server_auth_token.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Pingcore?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 18, 2026, alternatives to Pingcore in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.
Pingcore requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Pingcore is developed by Thinkhuge. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
